findings.title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates connectedCalendars, leaving stale cache status in the UI
findings.body: The `deleteCache` mutation only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. Unlike the `disconnectMutation` right below it (which invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in `onSettled`), nothing refetches the connected calendars query after the cache rows are deleted. `cacheUpdatedAt` is derived server-side from `CalendarCache.updatedAt`, so after a successful delete the dropdown continues to show "Cache Status / Last updated …" and the "Delete cached data" item, and the user can "delete" again indefinitely. This is only masked when the parent happens to pass an `onChanged` that invalidates the query, which `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` does not guarantee (`onChanged` is optional and not passed from every call site, e.g. event-type settings). Add `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in `onSettled`/`onSuccess` of `deleteCacheMutation`.

findings.title: Authorization failure throws a plain Error, surfacing as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
findings.body: When the credential does not exist or does not belong to the session user, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps non-`TRPCError` exceptions to a 500 `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, so a client probing other users' credential IDs gets a server-error response (and the error is logged/reported as an unexpected failure) instead of a proper `NOT_FOUND`/`FORBIDDEN`. Other handlers in this router family use `TRPCError` with an explicit code; this one should too.

findings.title: Cache status ignores expiresAt, so expired (unusable) cache rows are reported as live cache
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows by `credentialId` and returns `max(updatedAt)` without filtering on `expiresAt`. `getCachedAvailability` in the same file only ever serves rows with `expiresAt >= now`, so rows that expired are never used for availability. The UI nevertheless shows "Cache Status – Last updated <date>" and offers "Delete cached data" for credentials whose only cache rows are expired, which misrepresents whether caching is actually in effect. Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the `where` clause (or expose the expiry so the UI can distinguish).

findings.title: Unneeded updateMany on every webhook touches all SelectedCalendar rows and can fail the webhook after cache was written
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now ends with `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`, an UPDATE of every `SelectedCalendar` row (user-level and all event-type-level rows) for the credential, solely to bump `updatedAt`. This runs on every Google push notification (hot path) and also from `unwatchCalendar`. Nothing in this PR reads `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` — the UI uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt` — and the PR description itself notes it is unused. Besides the write amplification, the call is outside any try/catch: if it fails (e.g. lock contention) the webhook handler errors after the cache has already been upserted, causing Google to retry a webhook whose actual work succeeded. Remove the call or make it best-effort.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires unused updatedAt/googleChannelId fields on selected calendars
findings.body: `UserWithCalendars.allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` are widened to require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`, which forced `findUnlockedUserForSession` in `packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts` to select those columns into the session user. No code in this PR consumes either field (`connectedCalendarsHandler` derives `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCache`, not from `SelectedCalendar`). The change tightens the input contract of `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` for every caller (platform-libraries/API v2, tests that build user fixtures) and grows the per-request session payload with per-calendar channel IDs, for no functional benefit. Revert the type widening and the extra `select` fields.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded en-US locale
findings.body: The "Last updated" timestamp is rendered with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` while the surrounding strings come from `useLocale()`. Non-English users see an English date/time format (MM/DD/YY, 12-hour clock) embedded in a translated sentence, and the user's configured timezone is not considered. Use the active locale from `useLocale()` (e.g. `i18n.language`) and, ideally, the user's timezone as other date displays in the app do.

findings.title: No tests for the new deleteCache authorization or the cache-status enrichment
findings.body: The PR adds a destructive, user-facing mutation (`deleteCacheHandler`) whose only guard is a `credential.userId === user.id` lookup, a new repository method (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), and a change to `connectedCalendarsHandler`'s response shape (`cacheUpdatedAt`), but includes no unit or integration tests. In particular there is no test asserting that a user cannot delete another user's `CalendarCache` rows, that deletion scopes to the given `credentialId` only, or that `cacheUpdatedAt` is populated/null as expected. The PR description admits local testing was not possible. Add handler tests (e.g. with prismock as used elsewhere in `packages/trpc`) covering the deny path and the enrichment mapping.

findings.title: Script uses macOS-only `sed -i ''` and a CWD-relative .env path
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E "s|…|…|" "$ENV_FILE"` is BSD/macOS syntax; on GNU sed (Linux, CI, devcontainers) `''` is parsed as the sed script and the substitution expression is treated as a filename, so the command fails and `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is never updated. Additionally `ENV_FILE="../.env"` (line 5) is resolved relative to the caller's working directory rather than the script's location, so running `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root creates/edits a `.env` outside the repository. Resolve the path from `$(dirname "$0")` and use a portable in-place edit (e.g. write to a temp file and `mv`).

findings.title: dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` but tsx is not a declared dependency
findings.body: `dev:cron` now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, yet `tsx` is not listed in `dependencies` or `devDependencies` (only `ts-node` is). `npx` will try to download an unpinned latest `tsx` at run time, requiring network access and yielding non-reproducible behavior across machines/CI. This change is also unrelated to the calendar-cache feature. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency and call it directly, or keep the `ts-node` invocation.

findings.title: Removed `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` check from findMany without justification
findings.body: `findMany` previously built its args with `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs`, which guaranteed the hand-written `FindManyArgs` type (kept narrow to avoid an atoms build TS crash, per the comment above it) stays compatible with Prisma's real argument type. The PR drops that assertion and passes the object directly. Since the call still type-checks against Prisma, the removal is unnecessary, and it silently removes the guard that would catch future drift between `FindManyArgs` and Prisma's types. This is also unrelated to the feature.

findings.title: Migration header warning contradicts the statement that follows
findings.body: The auto-generated comment says the column is added "without a default value" and that this "is not possible if the table is not empty", but the actual statement adds `DEFAULT NOW()` precisely so existing rows are handled. The stale warning is misleading for anyone auditing migrations and should be removed or corrected.
